I was very athletic when I was younger and for some reason my brain still thinks that my body will move in ways that it will no longer move. It is so frustrating to be playing a sport or just goofing off and you expect a certain movement but your body just slugs it's way though the motion. It's like being trolled by your own body.

I look forward to being able to move like I perceive that I can.
BFS because my brain still thinks I am skinny...

I hear that.

I used to play a lot of sports, always weighed in a little hefty. But over the years I ended up with too many big injuries and I couldn't play anything anymore. Then I got fatter. With that my kees started to self destruct to the point where I could barely walk up stairs, which lead to more sitting around and getting fatter.

I started some physio a few months ago to strengthen my lower body and it really started to help. I'm making some of those old moves like you described and I'm still surprised when I don't just fall over.

Take it slow, make real progress, make it part of your life, and feel good again.
Between volleyball, tennis, cheerleading, and snowboarding I had knee issues even before I gained weight. I probably should see PT. How much of a time investment is it?

It's not huge. I started at going once a week to suss out the problem and learn some exercises, maybe a half hour appointment. Over the next week I would do the exercises at least once a day for 10 minutes or so. After the week I would head back to talk about what happened, what hurt, where does it hurt now, what felt good. They also wanted to see if I was still doing things proper. Then we'd figure out new things to try.

After a few weeks I would pop in once every 2-3 weeks to check progress. Since we were able to find the right exercises to target the problems, I was told to just keep it up and only come back if there's a problem.

My commitment to the exercises also went down over time because I was able to make a good base at the start, and could spread out my sessions to once every few days. Right now I'm at once a week or so but I can feel things slipping back so I need to re-up my effort.

I didn't start the physio first thing. The first thing I did was check in with my doctor. I got an x-ray to check for stray bone fragments. There were a few but they weren't getting in the way with my regular movements. One of the exercises I tried early on in the physio cause a fragment to wedge itself in somewhere painful, so I stopped doing that one.

After the x-ray I ended up with a CT scan to check if there was any soft tissue damage or if I had any left. I had some damage but nothing worth digging for until I tried physio.

It seems to be working for now and got me moving again which was nice. I almost cried one day when I walked up some stairs and didn't feel any pain. That was a great day.

Side note: I tried doing it myself first from youtube videos, really did not work and I wouldn't recommend that.

Good luck!
